Milwaukee firm Rapid Radicals plans Great Lakes rollout of water tech
Rapid Radicals plans to deploy its patented wastewater treatment technology in major Midwest and coastal cities in the coming years.
A Milwaukee-based company called Rapid Radicals plans to roll out its wastewater treatment technology in major Midwest cities and coastal communities over the coming years, following the company's securing of a patent for the technology late last year, according to founder and Chief Technology Officer Paige Peters.
Peters spoke about the company's plans Tuesday, Oct. 6, during the Wisconsin Technology Council's Launch Wisconsin conference at Marquette University in Milwaukee.
The company offers a water treatment system packaged into a modular shipping container called the Torrent3. Along with reducing the footprint needed for municipal and industrial water treatment, the company says the system substantially reduces hauling and operational costs for customers. Rapid Radicals previously won the grand prize in the Wisconsin Governor's Business Plan Contest in 2022.
"I truly believe that it can solve some really important problems," Peters said. "Seeing blue containers on … the five most important sewer overflow locations for the Great Lakes cities and coastal cities, seeing this deployed at industrial facilities where we can really help, like I said, solve problems and eliminate burden on municipalities."
Peters launched the company 10 years ago as a spin-off from Marquette University after developing a method for treating municipal wastewater 22 times faster than conventional treatment systems, according to the company. The business has since expanded into industrial wastewater treatment.
Peters said the wastewater treatment sector is capital-intensive, highly technical and slow to adopt new solutions. "We are trying to sell to a very slow-moving, risk-averse, long sales cycle industry, which means that timing can be incredibly unpredictable," she said, adding "there's statistics that say it takes 12 years for any sort of water technology to leave the lab and enter the market. We did it in nine years, so I feel really excited about that."
Source: WisPolitics, https://www.wisbusiness.com/2026/rapid-radicals-targeting-great-lakes-region-rollout-in-coming-years/
